layer_status.mcl-core: Provisional semantic normalization assignments and opcode registries, with seven currently implemented Tier-0 reference semantics. C validator with overflow and truncation hardening.
layer_status.mcl-wire: Freestanding C99 reference codec. Bit-level encode/decode for 7 Tier-0 semantics (PRESENCE, HAZARD, REQUEST, AUTHORITY_CLAIM, DEGRADED_STATE, TRANSPORT_OFFER, TRANSPORT_ACCEPT). TRANSPORT_OFFER and TRANSPORT_ACCEPT carry a 32-bit migration_ref transaction correlator. Extensions are now reachable from the Tier-0 API: mcl_wire_tier0_encode_ext and mcl_wire_tier0_decode_ext carry a canonical TLV block after the fixed body, specified in tier0-extensions-v0.1.md with vectors in extensions-v0.1.json. The block carries its own length so a Tier-0 object stays self-delimiting, which the raw-Wire path over AP requires. An empty extension list encodes with the bit clear and no block, so every existing vector is unchanged byte for byte. An unknown CRITICAL extension makes the whole object undecodable, and since no extension id is registered, every critical extension is currently unknown; a decoder that cannot read extensions refuses an object carrying them rather than returning the body and discarding the rest. No extension id is assigned and no extension registry policy exists yet, so extensions are usable only between parties that agreed an id out of band. Randomized fuzz decode. Versioned vectors: tier0-v0.1/v0.2/v0.3, none edited after publication. Zero heap allocation.
layer_status.mcl-link: C99 reference state machine (9-state lifecycle, context install/authorize/compare, wire major mask without narrowing); the Link frame v0 canonical layout, 8 bytes minimum, flag-selected destination/session/sequence/freshness/CRC-32 frame check, with truncation reported distinctly from permanent malformation; a contact-migration state machine (ACTIVE/OFFERED/AGREED/VALIDATING/VALIDATED/COMMITTING) with transaction correlation, candidate-path validation before commit, and deterministic simultaneous-offer resolution; the transport-neutral rendezvous beacon that resolves an endpoint_token to a concrete endpoint; and the canonical HANDOFF control payload (link-handoff-control-v0.1.md, operation registry handoff-ops-v0.1.json, vectors handoff-v0.1.json) that puts PATH_CHALLENGE, PATH_RESPONSE, COMMIT and CONFIRM on the wire as bytes rather than as local function calls. A COMMIT that repeats a completed transaction is answered with CONFIRM again and changes nothing, because without that a single dropped CONFIRM leaves the two peers on different transports permanently with no adversary involved. No ABORT operation is assigned; negative outcomes are expressed by absence and by the caller-enforced offer validity. Migration is deliberately non-cryptographic: it establishes correlation and reachability, never identity.
layer_status.mcl-sdk: C99 reference SDK. Node init/reset, Tier-0 send/receive over raw Wire bytes, and a framed contact path over Link frames for the IP/BLE/UWB bindings. Transmit sequence advances only on transport success; a session reference comes from the contact and requires an agreed migration, never from the Wire context_id; malformed frames are rejected before semantic decoding; reception has zero side effects on link state. A handoff control path sends, receives and applies the Link HANDOFF controls as three separate steps: receiving decodes and changes nothing, and applying is an explicit caller decision that drives the existing mcl_contact_* API rather than a duplicate state machine. A control carried in any frame class other than HANDOFF, or in a frame whose session_ref contradicts its payload, is refused. tests/test_sdk_handoff.c completes a migration between two nodes whose only shared object is a byte buffer, including recovery from a CONFIRM dropped after a successful send. Zero heap allocation, caller-owned buffers.
layer_status.mcl-ap: Analytical channel model (ISO 9613-1); Experiment 001 (LAB/EXPERIMENTAL hosted binary FSK testbed, frozen at 3/5 kHz as the instrument holding the E3 result); Experiment 002 part A (real transducer path characterization); Experiment 003 (band-informed AP-B0 candidate, 3/6 kHz, with a same-session control and a reverse-direction E4 result). No normative profile. AP-B0 NOT selected. Protocol-facing Wire, Link, and SDK libraries remain freestanding C99.
layer_status.mcl-ip: Reference implementation. Endpoint offer with family-consistent address sizing and an opaque local reference so first contact need not force address disclosure; datagram carriage where the datagram boundary is the frame boundary; length-prefixed stream carriage that preserves synchronisation across an undecodable frame; MTU accounting; a rendezvous discovery datagram that resolves an endpoint_token to a concrete address, on the provisional unregistered port 49913. Freestanding C99, no sockets, no libc symbols.
layer_status.mcl-ble: Reference implementation. Fixed-size endpoint offer; explicit fragmentation and reassembly for the 20-byte default ATT payload, with START/END/sequence framing that discards rather than splices on loss, reordering, orphaned continuations or restart; connectionless presence confirmed to fit 31-byte advertising data; a rendezvous advertising structure carrying the beacon in Service Data for the MCL 128-bit service UUID, with an AD walk that tolerates arbitrary scan results. Freestanding C99, no Bluetooth stack, no libc symbols.
layer_status.mcl-uwb: Reference implementation. Fixed-size endpoint offer; one Link frame per UWB data frame; ranging-evidence record that deliberately exposes no verified distance and no proximity-proved flag. Admissibility as proximity evidence requires performed ranging, a drift-cancelling method, authenticated scrambled timestamps and moderate radio confidence; overflow in distance conversion is refused rather than wrapped. No distance bounding is implemented or claimed. Freestanding C99, no UWB driver, no libc symbols.

C0_static_registry.detail: semantic-codes-v0.2.json validated by tools/validate_registry.c with overflow and truncation hardening.

C1_canonical_encoding.detail: 7 Tier-0 semantics encode/decode bit-perfectly. Vectors retained in mcl-wire/tests/test_vectors.c and conformance/vectors/tier0-v0.3.json; the v0.1 and v0.2 vector files remain exactly as published.

C2_negative_decoding.detail: Truncated, malformed-opcode, noncanonical-padding, and oversized inputs tested. Randomized fuzz_decode exercised.

C3_link_state_tests.detail: 9-state lifecycle transitions, context install/reject in forbidden states, wire major mask boundary (0..UINT32_MAX), context compare. Contact migration adds the HANDOFF control codec with published vectors (handoff-v0.1.json): positive vectors for all four operations, negative vectors for truncation, trailing bytes, reserved/unassigned/Experimental operations, wrong control version, and zero migration_ref or session_ref, plus exhaustive sweeps of the whole one-byte operation and control-version spaces. State-level negatives cover stale migration_ref, foreign session_ref, wrong challenge echo, COMMIT before VALIDATED, CONFIRM before COMMITTING, and duplicate COMMIT after completion.

C4_independent_interoperability.detail: No independent implementation exists to test against.

C6_device_ecosystem_robustness.detail: Three transport families have now run between two physically distinct machines: acoustic (mcl-ap), 2.4 GHz UDP (mcl-ip) and Bluetooth LE (mcl-ble). Each run included deliberate malformed input and each peer refused it as specified. This is device diversity across transports, not ecosystem scale: one board model, one host, no third-party peer, and no multi-node contention testing.

C5_transport_profile_conformance.detail: mcl-ip and mcl-ble carriage rules were exercised over real radios against a second machine. IP: datagram boundary equals frame boundary, trailing bytes refused, truncation distinguished from malformation, future major version reported as unsupported. BLE: fragmentation and reassembly at the minimum 23-byte MTU, with gap, orphan, non-canonical START and post-refusal recovery all verified. No normative profile is defined for either binding, so this is evidence toward a future C5 rather than a C5 pass. AP remains NOT_RUN because AP-B0 is not selected.

E0_analytical.detail: ISO 9613-1 attenuation, spherical spreading, Doppler, serialization time, bitrate-equal-to-propagation. Boundary conditions tested (distance=0, negative, payload=0).

E1_deterministic_simulation.detail: Experiment 001: Binary FSK 300 baud, 48 kHz mono PCM, 4 preamble candidates (LFM chirp, Zadoff-Chu derived, PN m-sequence, frequency-diverse) evaluated with exact length invariant (N=4800, 0.1s), verified 7-bit m-sequence (period 127), equalized energy budgets, quadrature correlation magnitude, and preliminary small-sample empirical Pfa threshold calibration (target Pfa=0.010, exactly 100 noise trials per candidate). Corrected impairment harness with explicit enablement: measured AWGN power verified across 30, 20, 10, 5, 0 dB (at 0 dB SNR, noise power equals signal power within 0.5% and P_d=1.000, 12/12 payload CRC valid); post-filter colored noise power measured and scaled to requested SNR (30, 20, 15, 10, 5, 0 dB); band attenuation verified via pure sine probes (3000, 3800, 4000, 4200, 5000 Hz) with measured center notch attenuation of exactly -10.00 dB at 4000 Hz; hardened RIFF WAV chunk scanner and strict format rejection. Experiment 001 is a host-side research testbed using hosted C math/stdio/WAV; the protocol-facing Wire/Link/SDK C libraries remain freestanding C99. Experiment 003 adds a band-informed candidate that changes only the FSK mark tone (5000 -> 6000 Hz) on the measurement from Experiment 002 part A; against a same-session 3000/5000 control it took exact recovery from 0/10 to 9/10 on the DFR1154 receiver and 0/10 to 4/10 on the laptop Realtek receiver.

E2_replay.detail: Retained physical capture evidence/e3-dfr1154-20260902/capture-005-crc-verified.wav (DFR1154 ESP32-S3 PDM microphone, 48 kHz PCM16 mono, board CRC-32 DF6E6D65 verified host-side) replays through the offline decoder to valid frame CRC 0x219A, exact Wire bytes 00 02 00 00 00 01 01 00 00 01 3C, and exact PRESENCE semantic recovery. This required a receiver change made after the capture (symbol-boundary rounding rather than truncation), so it is replay evidence only and does NOT establish E3. Retained same-laptop Realtek captures still achieve no recovery.

E3_controlled_over_air_frame.detail: First over-air recovery of an exact MCL frame. The hashed source exp001_e3_source.wav was played through the laptop Realtek speaker and captured by the DFR1154 ESP32-S3 onboard PDM microphone at 48 kHz PCM16 mono, returned over native USB CDC with board-side IEEE CRC-32 verified host-side. Ten trials taken against the frozen receiver after the symbol-boundary rounding change, decoded with no further modification: 10/10 preamble acquisition (correlation 0.874086 to 0.877460), 10/10 PHY header recovery, 8/10 exact Wire bytes and exact PRESENCE semantic object. A separate 3-trial pilot under identical conditions recovered 3/3, giving 13 trials with 13/13 acquisition and 11/13 exact recovery. Both failures acquired cleanly and decoded all 24 header bits correctly, failing only on payload symbols; the measured cause is transducer response, the PDM microphone attenuating the 5 kHz mark tone approximately 12.4 dB relative to the 3 kHz space tone and leaving roughly 0.3 of log-energy decision margin on the weakest end-of-frame symbols. Evidence, per-trial table, and SHA-256 manifests are retained in mcl-ap under experiments/001-known-waveform/evidence/e3-dfr1154-20260902-frozen-rx and -frozen-rx-pilot. Same-laptop Realtek microphone attempts still achieve no recovery. This is single-operator, single-device-pair, short-range evidence; it is not multi-device (E4) and does not select AP-B0.

E4_multi_device.detail: First multi-device over-air recovery, in the reverse direction from E3. The DFR1154 MAX98357 amplifier and onboard speaker transmitted the Experiment 003 candidate frame (FSK 3000/6000 Hz) and the laptop Realtek microphone array received it: 10/10 preamble acquisition at correlation 0.883-0.889 and 8/10 exact Wire bytes plus exact PRESENCE semantic recovery; a 3-trial pilot recovered 1/3. Neither transducer is shared with E3 and the emitting device is now the embedded one. Acquisition on this path (0.883-0.889) is far stronger than laptop-speaker to laptop-microphone measured the same day (0.35-0.53) with the same microphone, which separates transmitter from receiver response and confirms the Experiment 002 finding that the notch is in the laptop speaker. Evidence in mcl-ap under experiments/003-band-informed-candidate/evidence/e4-board-speaker-to-laptop-mic-20260902/. Limits: the 3000/6000 pair was chosen from a forward-path sweep and this reverse path has not been swept; two physical devices in reversed roles rather than a third independent device; one operator, one room, one geometry, one session; AP-B0 remains NOT selected.

compiler_verification._note: Re-verified 2026-09-03. The gates are run BY HAND in TWO parts, and neither alone is 'the gates': mcl-core/tools/local-gates.sh covers GCC, Clang, ASan/UBSan, the two freestanding cross-compiles and the C++ header compiles, and mcl-core/tools/local-gates-msvc.ps1 covers MSVC. The shell script needs a POSIX shell and the GNU/LLVM toolchain and does NOT run MSVC; an earlier revision of this note claimed it ran 'every gate below in one pass', which overstated the coverage. This project has no hosted CI and will not gain any: a governing interoperability layer whose verification depends on one vendor's build service has a dependency it did not declare. Passing establishes nothing about physical evidence.

msvc_19_51.detail: All eight repositories compile and pass their full test suites under MSVC 19.51 with /W4 /WX. 30 test targets, counted by local-gates-msvc.ps1 from ctest's own summary rather than written from memory -- the count in this field was wrong twice before, in both directions, because it was typed. Run separately from the Linux gates.

gcc_13_strict.detail: All eight repositories compile and pass their full test suites under GCC 13.3.0 with -std=c99 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Wconversion -Wsign-conversion -Wshadow -Wundef -Werror.

clang_18_strict.detail: All eight repositories compile and pass their full test suites under Clang 18.1.3 with the same strict flag set. Clang's -Wunneeded-internal-declaration found a BLE test constant that was consumed only for its length while reading as though it carried a real PRESENCE frame; the test now carries the actual bytes and compares them after reassembly.

asan_ubsan.detail: ALL EIGHT repositories build and pass their full suites under Clang with -fsanitize=address,undefined and -fno-sanitize-recover=undefined. Previously only Core, Wire, Link and SDK were covered, which left out every binding parser -- the BLE advertising-data scanner and fragment reassembler, the IP endpoint and datagram/stream decoders, the UWB endpoint and ranging decoders -- all of which read bytes chosen by a peer or by whatever else is transmitting nearby. Widening the coverage immediately found undefined behaviour in the AP experiment: exp001.c converted a negative double to size_t during the timing search (UBSan: '-16 is outside the range of representable values of type unsigned long'). Every call site rejects a negative boundary with its own test, but that test ran after the conversion, so the undefined conversion happened and its result was discarded. Fixed and re-verified: the retained E3 source still decodes to the exact same Wire bytes and semantic object.

arm_cortex_m0.detail: wire.c, extension.c, link.c, contact.c, rendezvous.c, handoff.c, sdk.c and the IP/BLE/UWB bindings compiled with --target=arm-none-eabi -mcpu=cortex-m0 -mthumb -std=c99 -Os -ffreestanding -fno-builtin -Werror. llvm-nm reports no memcpy, memset, malloc, free or stdio symbol in any object. wire.o, link.o, contact.o, rendezvous.o and handoff.o have zero undefined externals. ble_binding.o and uwb_binding.o each reference __aeabi_uidiv, because Cortex-M0 has no divide instruction and both perform a division on a runtime value; per IMPLEMENTATION_CONTRACT.md 2.2 an AEABI compiler-runtime helper is a toolchain artifact rather than a libc dependency, so an integrator targeting this core links compiler-rt or libgcc as is normal for freestanding ARM. RV32IM needs no such helper because the M extension provides hardware divide.

riscv32_rv32im.detail: The same translation units compiled with --target=riscv32-none-elf -march=rv32im -mabi=ilp32 -std=c99 -Os -ffreestanding -fno-builtin -Werror. llvm-nm reports no libc symbol and no compiler-runtime helper in any object; every undefined external is an mcl_* symbol from a lower layer.

cpp_headers.detail: Every public header compiles together in one C++17 translation unit under both g++ and clang++ with -Wall -Wextra -Werror, since integrators embed these headers in C++ sources.

codebase_status.summary: All eight repositories contain implementation, not only specification. 30 test targets pass across the family under MSVC, GCC and Clang with warnings as errors, and all eight pass under ASan and UBSan.
codebase_status.freestanding_verification: Link, Wire, SDK, IP, BLE and UWB objects compiled and inspected for undefined externals: no memcpy, memset, malloc or stdio. Byte copies use a volatile-destination helper because optimising compilers rewrite plain indexed loops into memcpy, which would reintroduce a libc dependency.
not_implemented: ACK, NACK, KEEPALIVE and CLOSE now have codecs (mcl-link/include/mcl/control.h). What they do NOT have is a caller: nothing in the SDK sends or acts on one yet, so the frame classes are specified and encodable and not yet part of any exchange. ADAPT is reserved and now rejected by both encoder and decoder. CAPABILITY and NEGOTIATION remain provisional pending the capability and version/context controls.

No Wire extension id is assigned and no extension registry policy exists. The decoder now lets a caller decide which critical ids it implements AND whether it accepts each value (mcl_wire_tier0_decode_ext_accept), so a registry can be added without changing the decode contract -- but the registry itself must still state owner, range policy, application procedure, change controller, provisional-to-permanent promotion, deprecation behaviour and the no-reuse rule.

SIXTEEN of the twenty-one Tier-0 field MEANINGS are not settled. The byte layouts are now authoritative and machine-checked (mcl-wire/spec/tier0-layout-v0.2.md, verified against the codec in both directions by mcl_wire_validate_tier0_layout), but 10 fields are provisional and 6 are open -- recorded field by field in mcl-core/registries/tier0-fields-v0.1.json. The most serious is that HAZARD and REQUEST coordinates have NO defined frame of reference: no origin, no axis convention, no quantization. If they require an external frame to interpret then those two are not context-free Tier-0 objects, which is Tier-0's defining property. Bit-perfect decoding without shared meaning is not interoperability.

One mcl_node_t holds one contact. A machine needing several concurrent contacts instantiates several nodes. A caller-owned contact pool with no hidden allocation is the intended shape and is not built.
mcl-uwb has never been exercised against real UWB hardware, and no UWB profile is assigned.
No independent implementation exists, so C4 and E6 are unreachable by construction.
AP-B0 is not selected; no normative acoustic profile is defined.

No normative transport profile is defined for IP or BLE. Their profile registries assign Experimental Use values only, because the profiles are defined by reference-implementation behaviour rather than by specification.
No cryptographic capability of any kind exists. See security_posture.
The reverse acoustic path has never been swept with Experiment 002; the 3/6 kHz pair is optimised for the forward path only.
The semantic registry marks 15 opcodes as Tier-0 candidates while 7 are implemented. The registry must not imply executable support that does not exist.

The HANDOFF control assigns no ABORT operation. Convergence after a failed migration therefore depends on the caller enforcing the offer validity, since the library has no clock. This is a deliberate decision recorded in link-handoff-control-v0.1.md section 9, not an oversight, and it can be revisited by assigning an operation value without a version change.
MCL_IP_RENDEZVOUS_PORT 49913 is unregistered and provisional; this project holds no IANA assignment.
codebase_status.audit_2026_09_02: A file-by-file audit fixed seven defects that would otherwise have shipped: a compiler-synthesised memset in mcl-link that broke the freestanding contract; truncation conflated with permanent malformation in Link decode and then mistranslated by two bindings; a BLE reassembly bound below the largest legal Link frame; an unguarded fragment-sequence wrap; an unenforced exact payload boundary in the SDK; an unbounded IP stream length prefix; and an MTU accounting function that contradicted its own documented contract. Two session-scaffolding documents were removed and their durable content promoted to governance/IMPLEMENTATION_CONTRACT.md.
codebase_status.audit_2026_09_03: Acted on an external protocol review. Fixed the SDK emitting the Wire context_id as a frame's session_ref, two unrelated identifiers sharing an integer; a test had asserted that behaviour, which is why it survived. Added a migration transaction correlator, without which a delayed acceptance from an abandoned offer was indistinguishable from the live one. Added candidate-path validation, because acceptance is not arrival. Fixed a genuine deadlock where simultaneous offers left both peers rejecting and waiting. Defined endpoint_token resolution, without which a hardware migration would have proved only that the harness knew where the peer was. Created per-binding profile registries, because profile_id=1 meant nothing in three bindings and was about to fossilize.
closed_since_last_manifest: The SDK is transport-aware on both TX and RX. It could not model two simultaneous transports at all before, which made it the blocker ahead of any BLE<->IP hardware run: one tx callback with no transport argument cannot express a migration, and a receive path that does not know where bytes arrived cannot verify that a PATH_RESPONSE crossed the candidate.

The transmit callback reports three outcomes -- sent, definitely not sent, unknown -- and the SDK owns the COMMIT transition around the transmission. Collapsing the last two forces a choice between a contact stranded irrevocably in COMMITTING over a frame nobody sent, and a rollback after a commit the peer may have acted on.

Every migration control is now idempotent, not just COMMIT. The gap that mattered: a retransmitted PATH_CHALLENGE was refused because the peer had left AGREED, so one dropped frame killed a migration with both peers behaving correctly.
Ordinary traffic is quiesced between COMMIT and CONFIRM, instead of being sent onto a medium the peer may already have left.

MCL_LINK_FLAG_SESSION is mandatory on handoff frames, enforced on send and receive. It was a SHOULD checked only when present, which made the field a multi-contact receiver needs for routing optional.

mcl_contact_link_state is deleted. It claimed a mapping between two independently mutable state machines and so was a third source of truth that drifted from both. Ownership is decided in mcl-link/spec/link-contact-ownership-v0.1.md.
session_ref is decided to persist for the life of the contact, enforced rather than documented. The repeated-migration test had been asserting the opposite model by passing a new reference each hop.

The NACK reason set is corrected: five of the original reasons were unsendable, because a receiver rejecting a frame at those points cannot quote a trustworthy acked_sequence out of it. Sequence wrap now has a bounded window rather than a note saying the field wraps.

The authoritative Tier-0 body layout exists and is machine-checked against the codec, so a second implementation can be built without reading the reference C. Until now the only complete statement of the layouts was that C, which inverts the project's own rule.

Contact migration has crossed real radios. One ESP32-S3 holding a SoftAP with a UDP socket and a BLE GATT server up at the same time, and a Windows host holding both, each with a single mcl_node_t across the pair: 104 migrations, 2989 checks, 0 failed, host and board records agreeing frame for frame. Driven by on-wire HANDOFF controls, not by direct calls to mcl_contact_* -- which the previous manifest correctly said must never be recorded as on-wire migration. A valid control delivered on the old path was refused as WRONG_TRANSPORT, which is the check path validation depends on and which no single-transport rig can construct. See transport_evidence.migration.

transport_evidence.note: Evidence levels for the non-acoustic bindings, kept separate from ap_evidence because the ladder describes physical reality per transport and merging them would obscure which medium was used.

mcl-ip.detail: 2026-09-02. Windows host on a Realtek RTL8188EU USB adapter and an ESP32-S3 SoftAP peer, 2.4 GHz channel 6, one Link frame per UDP datagram. 28 checks, 0 failed, 0 retries. Host sent 111 datagrams, board received 111, accepted 103, refused 8, replied 111, zero loss in either direction. The eight refusals covered truncation, a trailing byte, an unknown class, a reserved bit, a future major version, a corrupted frame check, a corrupted payload and an overstated payload length.

mcl-ble.detail: 2026-09-02. Windows host over a MediaTek Bluetooth adapter and an ESP32-S3 peripheral, connectionless and connected. 35 checks, 0 failed, 20/20 sustained exchanges. Fragmentation was performed at MTU 23, the smallest BLE permits, rather than the large MTU Windows negotiates, which would have carried every test frame in a single PDU. Four malformed fragment sequences were discarded rather than spliced and recovery was then asserted; a fifth carried a frame with a corrupted frame check inside well-formed fragments, which reassembly accepted and Link refused one layer up. A 19-byte Tier-0 PRESENCE Link frame was also carried in the scan response and decoded by the host.

mcl-uwb.detail: Unit-tested C99 carriage mapping. Has never met UWB hardware.

transport_evidence.shared_limit: Both ends of every run compile the same mcl-link, mcl-wire and binding sources. A shared misreading of the specification would be accepted by both peers and would not appear in any of these results. None of this is independent interoperability.

migration.detail: 2026-09-03. The first MCL transport migration between two machines over real radios with BOTH media alive at the same time on both peers. A Windows host (MediaTek Bluetooth LE, Realtek RTL8188EU USB Wi-Fi) and one ESP32-S3 running a SoftAP with a UDP socket and a BLE GATT server simultaneously, each holding a single mcl_node_t across both. 104 migrations, including 100 consecutive alternating BLE<->IP cycles in 14.2 s; 2989 checks, 0 failed. Host and board records agree frame for frame -- 167 BLE frames and 161 datagrams sent, 167 and 161 received, no loss in either direction on either medium, logdrop=0. One session reference and one peer reference survived all 104 changes of medium. A valid frame and a valid PATH_CHALLENGE delivered on the wrong transport were both refused as WRONG_TRANSPORT: that is the check path validation depends on, and a single-transport rig cannot construct it at all. A deliberately destroyed COMMIT and a deliberately destroyed CONFIRM were each repaired by retransmission. The run found two defects, both fixed in the commits this manifest names: the SDK could not address a frame at all, and reserved profile 0 was accepted despite every registry calling it malformed.
migration.not_covered: Simultaneous offers and the exact tie (the board never initiates, so glare cannot arise on this rig), a wrong challenge echo (neither end can be made to lie without putting a lie in the shipped code), and endpoint resolution failure (on UDP the token resolves as "reply where the probe came from", so there is no lookup that can fail). All three are covered by unit tests only.

security_posture.scope: Security in MCL is an optional profile a deployment chooses, not a property of MCL itself. Deployments that broadcast to unknown listeners, and deployments whose peers already know each other by means outside MCL, are complete uses of the layer and are usable at this snapshot. The items below describe what is absent for deployments that do need it.
security_posture.provides_today: Nothing cryptographic. No confidentiality, no cryptographic authenticity, no peer authentication and no contact continuity exist in any repository.
security_posture.frame_check_rename: MCL_LINK_FLAG_INTEGRITY was renamed to MCL_LINK_FLAG_FRAME_CHECK, and MCL_LINK_ERR_INTEGRITY to MCL_LINK_ERR_FRAME_CHECK. The field is a CRC-32: it detects accidental corruption and provides no protection against deliberate modification, because an attacker recomputes it over the altered bytes. The wire bit is unchanged. This is an API-breaking rename taken deliberately while nothing is tagged, under Architecture Charter 2.11: a mechanism is never named for a property it does not provide.
security_posture.ble_run_caveat: The BLE evidence used Bluetooth Just Works pairing: encrypted against a passive listener, unauthenticated against an active one. No peer identity was established by that run.
security_posture.charter_additions: Charter 2.10 (MCL neither requires nor establishes trust: it must be usable between machines that already know each other as well as between strangers, and no transport, pairing or network join may by itself establish identity, authority or trust; where a security profile is in use across a transport migration, the new channel must be bindable to the original contact), 2.10.1 (the interaction sequence belongs to the deployment: disclosure order, migration, authentication, encryption and handoff are configuration, not protocol, and differently configured peers stay interoperable at the frame and semantic layers), 2.10.2 (MCL is not an authentication protocol; authentication is one thing it can be configured to carry) and 2.11 (security properties are separate and are never summarised into one indicator).
security_posture.correction_recorded: An earlier revision of the threat model proposed proving knowledge of a hash over the first-contact exchange. That is unsound: first contact is observable, so any listener computes the same value, and an attacker can bind a valid session of its own to a contact it merely watched. The corrected requirement is that a continuity proof depend on secret state both peers committed during the contact, which forces the key exchange to begin on the first medium and finish on the second.
